chunks: Whenever it was said: 'God's promise is certainly true, and there is no doubt about the Hour,' you replied: 'We know not what the Hour is. We have only a vague idea, but are not certain.'
ai.seo_question: How did the disbelievers respond to the reminder of the Hour and God's promise?
ai.summary: This verse captures the arrogant dismissal of the disbelievers who, when confronted with the certainty of the Resurrection, feigned ignorance of its timing while relying on mere conjecture (zann) rather than firm conviction (yaqin). In Shia exegesis, this highlights the spiritual stagnation of those who reduce divine promise to speculation, contrasting their uncertainty with the clarity of the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings on the inevitability of the Hour. It serves as a critique of superficial faith that acknowledges the concept but lacks the deep, certain knowledge required for true accountability.
